stances.claim: The SC's docket congestion has more than doubled from ~6,000 cases during CJ Panganiban's term to 14,491 cases by Dec 31, 2016, with new filings (6,526) outpacing disposals (1,028) -- meaning the backlog is structurally getting worse, not improving.
stances.rhetorical_move: comparative-historical-statistics (using CJ's own institutional memory as the prior benchmark)

stances.claim: The Court should reject outright all appeals which on their face are obviously unmeritorious -- following the US Supreme Court model where ~6,000 of 6,305 filings are facially dismissed, leaving only ~61 signed decisions per year and producing NO backlog.
stances.rhetorical_move: best-practice-import argument (US SC efficiency as benchmark)

stances.claim: Operation Zero Backlog -- the judicial 'bayanihan' during CJ Panganiban's term where justices with light caseloads voluntarily took surrendered old cases from a pool -- was a workable institutional mechanism that should be revived; its discontinuation after CJ retired was an inexplicable institutional regression.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-citation of prior institutional success + lament-of-discontinuation

notable_anecdotes: CJ Menon and his delegation of 11 Singapore justices and lawyers honoring CJ Panganiban's household with a courtesy call at his Makati home on April 12, 2019 -- a rare personal-hospitality detail that anchors the ASEAN Law Institute launch in face-to-face diplomatic ritual.

CJ's discovery of the 14,491 figure not from any internal SC memo but from reading 'its recent decision in Gio-Samar v. DOTC' -- meaning the Court's institutional self-awareness has become a matter of public-record candor rather than confidential management.

The naming of 'Operation Zero Backlog' as 'a kind of judicial bayanihan' -- applying the Filipino communal-labor concept to inter-justice case redistribution, a uniquely PH institutional metaphor for collegial court management.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban discloses the Supreme Court's own candid admission in Gio-Samar v. DOTC (March 12, 2019, ponente Justice Jardeleza) that as of December 31, 2016, the Court held 14,491 cases in its docket -- more than double the ~6,000 cases during his own CJ tenure -- with new filings of 6,526 outpacing the year's 1,028 disposals by decision or signed resolution. Each of the 15 justices averages 966 pending cases. He suggests the Court adopt the US Supreme Court's model of rejecting facially unmeritorious appeals outright (the US SC threw out ~6,000 of 6,305 filings in 2016 and issued only 61 signed decisions, eliminating its backlog), and calls for the revival of his own term's discontinued 'Operation Zero Backlog' -- a judicial bayanihan in which justices with light caseloads voluntarily took surrendered old cases from a pool. The column doubles as an announcement of the ASEAN Law Institute launch on April 13, 2019, at the New World Hotel Makati, hosted by FA Secretary Locsin Jr. with Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon (ALA president), CJ Bersamin, ES Medialdea, and CJ Panganiban as ALA Philippine Chapter chair, preceded by Menon's April 12 courtesy call at CJ's Makati home.
